Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

formal adjective

ceremonial, done with due form

also formally, a formal occasion, a formal dinner, formal words, ceremonial, solemn

classical

Cic. Dom. 122: omnia sollemnibus verbīs dīcere (Lewis & Short)
Cic. de Or. 3.197: sollemnēs epulae (Lewis & Short)

sollemnis, sollemne

adjective, third declension

solemn, ceremonial; fixed by custom

First “yearly”, of fixed religious rites; then of anything done with its proper ceremony, a festival, a feast, a form of words, a wedding (sollemne nūptiārum, Suet.); after Augustus also “usual, customary” (Lewis & Short). Sollemne as a noun is a rite or ceremony.

Examples

  • īte fēlīcēs, ait; celebrāte sine mē cursū sollemnem diem

    “Go, and good luck to you,” he said; “keep the festival day with a race, without me”Phaedr. App. 21.1–9

See also formal, celebrate, practice, official.

SourcesLewis & Short: sollemnis
